submission_text: ===PAGE 1=== # Bench voltage monitor: problem and scope  This report describes a bench-only prototype that warns an undergraduate electronics demonstrator when a 5 V teaching supply remains outside 4.75鈥?.25 V for two consecutive samples. The affected users are demonstrators supervising several workstations. A transient excursion should not interrupt an otherwise valid experiment. The testable gap is whether two-sample confirmation reduces transient false alarms without missing persistent excursions in a fixed simulated trace. This is not a safety-certified monitor.  ===PAGE 2=== # Method and implementation  Iteration 1 parses timestamped voltage samples and rejects missing values. Iteration 2 implements the two-sample confirmation rule, resetting the counter after an in-range sample. Iteration 3 presents a warning and a timestamped event log. A sensor adapter accepts either a CSV fixture or a hardware reader behind the same read_sample interface; the state machine does not depend on a sensor vendor. Unit tests cover boundary values, reset behaviour and a persistent low-voltage condition.  ===PAGE 3=== # Evaluation procedure  The fixture contains ten observations, sampled one second apart: 5.00, 4.60, 5.00, 4.60, 4.60, 5.00, 5.00, 5.40, 5.00, 5.00 V. Its persistent-event reference is the consecutive low pair at seconds 4鈥?; seconds 2 and 8 are isolated excursions. Compare the proposed rule with a one-sample threshold on this identical trace. Count detected persistent events, false alarm events and detection delay from the first persistent sample. Additional tests will exercise missing samples and a high-voltage pair. This manually constructed fixture is development data; no independent hardware experiment has been run.  ===PAGE 4=== # Results and discussion  For the stated trace, the one-sample threshold starts alarms at seconds 2, 4 and 8. The confirmation rule starts one alarm at second 5. Both detect the persistent event; false alarms decrease from two to zero, with one second of added delay. These are direct calculations on the toy sequence, not real equipment measurements. The trade-off follows from waiting for a second out-of-range sample. A supply failure requiring immediate shutdown would make that delay unacceptable. The tiny constructed sequence cannot establish field reliability.  # Figure 1. State-machine overview  In-range 鈫?reset counter; first out-of-range 鈫?pending; second out-of-range 鈫?warning. Throughout this report, an observation is a single sample and an alarm event starts only when entering the warning state.
rationale: Users and scope are clear. The report tests whether two consecutive readings reduce false alarms without missing lasting voltage changes.

submission_text: ===PAGE 1=== # Shared battery logger: opening note  Laboratory demonstrators need to find why a portable teaching battery stops during a session. The logger records voltage once per minute. We want its event list to identify an interruption of more than two minutes; shorter gaps are outside the current scope. The intended users are demonstrators, rather than students estimating battery lifetime.  ===PAGE 2=== # Appendix A: file contract  Rows have timestamp, voltage and status columns. A replay reader uses the same interface as the device reader. In the first increment we checked malformed CSV headers. A later increment added gap grouping. We have not recorded the result of either check. The work plan says to test the grouping rule using a stored fixture after the interface is stable.  ===PAGE 3=== # Equipment inventory  The demonstration kit contains one rechargeable pack, a USB cable and a voltage divider. Packing instructions ask the custodian to count these items at the end of the week. This inventory describes the kit, not a validation dataset.  ===PAGE 4=== # Discussion before measurements  The design is inexpensive and may make a missed sample easier to investigate. No run log or numeric results are available in this draft. A gap could arise from either an unplugged reader or the battery itself, so an interruption cannot be interpreted as battery failure without additional information. We use outage, gap and stop as informal names for a missing-data interval.  ===PAGE 5=== # Appendix B: unfinished checks  Possible measures are detection accuracy and processing time. The draft does not identify a labelled dataset, comparison method, sample count or acceptance threshold. The intended workflow is to read rows, reject invalid timestamps, group missing intervals and display the groups. It still needs a rule for clock resets. Diagram placeholder: add the final signal chart here.
rationale: Users and scope are identified, but no testable question is given. The two-minute threshold is unclear, and gaps cannot show causes.
